## How Runpod pricing works

Runpod pricing is based on the type of GPU workload you run. Pods are dedicated GPU instances for development and long-running jobs, Serverless bills inference workers based on usage, and Clusters support multi-node workloads and reserved capacity.

Storage and deployment choices affect total cost, so teams should choose the model that matches workload duration, traffic pattern, and control needs.

highlights:
Of eight GPU clouds read on 24 October 2026, Runpod’s Community Cloud lists the lowest rate for an RTX 4090, at $0.34 an hour. Its H100 PCIe, at $1.99, is the lowest by one cent.

Vast.ai’s cheapest verified hosts undercut every list price on the 5090, L40S, A100 and RTX PRO 6000. Its RTX PRO 6000 is $1.08 against Runpod’s $1.69. Vast.ai figures count its verified hosts only.

On our own Runpod account on 17 October 2026, one 1280 x 1280 FLUX 3 Klein image took about 28.5 seconds on a Secure Cloud RTX 4090. At that tier’s rate it costs $0.007 of GPU time an image.
